analysis.title: K-shaped construction: AI builds, housing stalls
key_insights: US private data-center construction spending hit USD96.5bn annualized in September, 90% above a year earlier and over ten times 2019. It is 12.2% of private non-residential construction.

Total US construction spending is -2.7% y/y in September but -4.8% excluding data centers. The segment is both the main support of the cycle and a concentration risk. A flattening of data-center spending would push the whole category to -3 to -3.5% a year.

Europe's data-center build is far smaller. FLAP-D hubs have about 1.4 GW under construction against 66-80 GW in the US, and just over 750 MW should be added across Europe in 2026, with power the main constraint.

Three constraints on data centers: labor (79% of North American markets report shortages, over 93% in Europe), power (PJM gas projects deliver 2030-2031), and politics (opposition to a local data center rose from 42% to 75% in one poll).

After the Democratic midterm sweep, Allianz does not expect the cycle to end. Texas and New York pauses could be reinforced, turning a cost constraint into a volume constraint by 2028. About 30 GW of 2028 capacity sits in states where a pause-favoring candidate was running.

2027 data-center volumes look secure, since about three-quarters of the 33.8 GW expected to be delivered is already under construction. Hyperscalers can absorb the costs while smaller developers and projects without secured power are most exposed.
The new tightening cycle hits housing. ECB deposit rate is 2.50% and the Fed range is 3.75%-4%. Allianz expects three more Fed hikes to 4.50-4.75% and two more ECB hikes to 3.00%.

US mortgage rates track the 10-year yield (correlation 0.89 in monthly changes) and not the Fed Funds target (0.13). The mortgage rate rose from 6.05% to 7.33% and the 10-year from 4.1% to 5.1%, mostly through real yields with breakevens barely changed.

US housing is weak. Starts were 1.22mn in September, 7.4% below a year earlier, builder sentiment is 29, unsold new homes equal 8.4 months of supply and 43% of builders cut prices. Starts are expected at 1.25-1.30mn in 2027-2028.

Europe's residential picture is uneven. Spanish permits are over twice their 2019 level, German permits are a third below 2019, and French permits are falling. Order-book balances are -37.0 in France and -24.8 in Germany. Euro area housing-loan demand fell a net -15% in Q3 with -27% expected in Q4.

US non-residential construction ex data centers is down -3.9% y/y. Offices ex data centers are -8.4% and warehouses -8.0%. Manufacturing is -17.9% as the chip-plant building phase ends. Industrial real estate fundamentals point to a trough in 2027.

Infrastructure is a buffer and not a boom. US public construction is +1.0% y/y, and highway real volumes are down about 7% after input costs rose 11.5%. The surface-transportation extension expires 11 December. France public works are forecast -8% in 2026 and -7% in 2027, while Germany's EUR500bn fund ramps slowly.
Cost pressure is intense. Copper is USD14,154 a ton, about 60% above January 2025, and US steel mill products are up 49% since January 2025. European construction input-price PMI peaked near 80.

Insolvencies are rising. 51 of 376 large-company cases in the first nine months of 2026 were in construction. Allianz expects global insolvencies +1% in 2027, with leveraged housing and conventional commercial developers most exposed.
Baseline US 10-year yield is 5.00% at end-2026, 4.75% at end-2027 and 4.25% in 2028. A pause in hyperscaler capex would remove the one growing construction segment.

sector_views.rationale: Strongest segment in 2027-28 with consensus growth of +33% in 2026 and +25% in 2027, and contractors can reprice, but labor, power and politics limit scale.
Weakest segment in both regions in 2027-28 on high long yields, weak demand and rising costs, with elevated insolvencies in Europe.

sector_views.sector: Conventional commercial and office real estate
sector_views.rationale: Tight credit, structurally lower office demand and spare factory capacity keep projects on hold. US office construction is expected to fall 4.5% in 2027.
Supportive but not booming. Utilities and power drive growth, while real highway volumes fall and EU recovery money ends.
Private power construction is a record USD172bn (+12.1%), generator backlogs run late into the decade and pricing power shifts to firms with skilled labor and equipment slots.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Data centers are masking a broader contraction in US construction.
Housing recovery has stalled as mortgage rates rose.
Up from 6.05% in February and driven by long yields, cutting affordability like a 14% price rise.
Real-yield move with breakevens at 2.35%, pricing tighter money for longer.
Allianz expects hikes in December, January and March, then easing to 3.75% by end-2028.
Two more hikes expected, then easing to 2.25% by end-2028.
Allianz baseline implies only gradual relief for property and housing.
Muted growth with residential the weakest segment.
About 60% above January 2025, adding to cost pressure.

risk_factors: Hyperscaler capex pause would remove the one growing construction segment.
State-level data-center moratoria in Texas, New York, Ohio and Georgia could become volume constraints by 2028.
Labor shortages, power equipment backlogs and grid connection delays cap data-center delivery.
Further rise in long yields would worsen housing and commercial real estate project viability.
Rising input costs (copper, steel, aluminum, cement) and tariffs, with weak demand preventing pass-through.
Elevated insolvencies among leveraged European developers and contractors.
US surface-transportation funding lapse after the extension ends 11 December.

Figure 6: 12-month rolling correlation between long-term yields and mortgage rates for the US, Germany, France, Spain, Italy and the euro area.
Figure 2B: data centers' share of metered electricity consumption in Ireland, 23% in 2025 versus 5% in 2015.
geopolitical: Democratic sweep in the 3 November US midterms with data centers a key issue, raising state-level restrictions in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Arizona.
War in the Middle East lifted energy prices and put monetary policy back on a tightening path, and disrupted energy and aluminum supply.
Tariffs and reshoring announcements are swing factors for US factory construction and for materials costs.
The war in Ukraine and Red Sea disruptions drove the earlier inflation shock.
EU recovery fund payments must be completed by 31 December 2026, creating a 2027 headwind for Italy and Spain.

tension_points.bull_case: Spending is up 90% y/y, consensus expects +33% in 2026 and +25% in 2027, 2027 volumes are largely under construction and contractor backlogs are expanding.
tension_points.bear_case: Labor, power and political limits, including Texas and New York pauses, could turn cost constraints into volume constraints by 2028, and the segment is a concentration risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A pause in hyperscaler capex, or lasting legislated moratoria in Texas or other large states, would break the bull case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Data centers remain the strongest construction segment and support the cycle, though labor, power and politics limit scaling.
theme_stances.evidence: The segment is both the main support of the cycle and a concentration risk.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising long yields explain the whole mortgage rate increase and keep residential the weakest segment in 2027-28.
theme_stances.evidence: long yields explain the entire increase
